stem: According to the findings of the LEAP study, what is the most effective approach to preventing peanut allergy in high-risk infants?

options.text: Early introduction before one year of age followed by regular consumption until five years of age.
Strict avoidance of all peanut products until the child reaches five years of age.
Introducing peanut products only after the child has successfully tolerated all other common allergens.
Occasional exposure to peanut protein once every few months to maintain tolerance.

explanation: The study demonstrated that sustained consumption starting in infancy significantly reduced allergy incidence compared to avoidance.
rationale: Consider the duration and frequency of intake mentioned as key factors in the landmark 2015 study.

optionExplanations.A: The study demonstrated that sustained consumption starting in infancy significantly reduced allergy incidence compared to avoidance.
optionExplanations.B: Historically recommended, the LEAP study actually proved that prolonged exclusion increases the risk of developing an allergy.
optionExplanations.C: There is no evidence that the order of allergen introduction affects the prevention of peanut allergy specifically.
optionExplanations.D: The study emphasized regular and sustained consumption rather than infrequent exposure.

source.hint: Consider the duration and frequency of intake mentioned as key factors in the landmark 2015 study.
